description: IETF Internet-Draft (filed March 2, 2026) proposing a model for AI agent authentication and authorization by extending existing standards — OAuth 2.0 and WIMSE (Workload Identity in Multi-System Environments) — rather than defining new protocols. Currently at version -00 (first draft). Submitted to the OAuth Working Group.
agents: Standards framework covering agent-to-agent auth delegation chains
Agent identity management (treating agents as workloads)
Authorization scoping at token-issuance time (vs PP's action-time)

funding.notes: IETF working document. No commercial entity or funding. Expires September 3, 2026 if not progressed.

pp_fit.feature: PP solves what this draft cannot — action-time authorization receipts vs token-issuance-time delegation
pp_fit.integration_complexity: strategic — PP should align with or extend this framework, not compete with it
pp_fit.urgency: medium — standards timelines are slow (6-18 months), but early shaping is valuable
pp_fit.key_gap: This draft extends OAuth: authorize at token-issuance time. PP authorizes at action-execution time and issues receipts. These are complementary — OAuth handles who can act (identity), PP handles what was authorized per action (authorization receipt). PP could position as the action-layer complement to this standard.
pp_fit.strategic_opportunity: Engage IETF OAuth WG as a contributor. Position PP's authorization receipt model as the 'action plane' complement to WIMSE's 'identity plane'. Submitting a PP-authored companion draft would establish Rod/PP as standards-setters, not just a startup.

notes: Not a competitor in the commercial sense — a standards effort that validates the space. Key risk: if this draft gets adopted as the RFC, 'agent authorization' becomes synonymous with OAuth extension and PP's action-receipt model could be sidelined. Key opportunity: engage Kasselman (GitHub PieterKas) as a thought-partner, propose that PP's authorization receipt model fills the 'action-time evidence' gap explicitly called out in the draft's 'identify gaps' section. Rod should read the full draft. Flag for Rod review.
